messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Data Loss Prevention: Network data security integration with Azure Firewall
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview integrates Data Loss Prevention with Azure Firewall to protect sensitive network traffic, including text, files, and AI interactions. Rolling out from mid-November 2026 (preview) to late April 2027 (general availability), it enables automatic tenant activation, policy configuration, and enhanced risk management without disrupting existing policies.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Purview is expanding network layer data security controls with Azure Firewall. This integration helps organizations detect and protect sensitive data in supported network traffic, including text, files, and AI interactions. Organizations can apply Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies to traffic from servers, virtual machines, and other endpoints to help prevent unauthorized sharing with cloud applications through browsers, applications, and APIs.

Rollout schedule

  • Public Preview: We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late March 2027 and expect to complete by late April 2027.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention and Azure Firewall to protect sensitive data in network traffic

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
  • Azure Firewall
  • Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
  • Microsoft Defender

What will happen

  • This integration will become available automatically in your tenant as it rolls out.
  • Administrators can configure DLP policies to protect text and files sent and received through supported network traffic from servers, virtual machines, and other endpoints.
  • Policies can help prevent unauthorized sharing of sensitive data with cloud applications through browsers, applications, and APIs.
  • DLP policies can apply to traffic generated by background services and automated workloads.
  • The integration will provide activity signals to Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management to help identify risky user behavior.
  • Alert management and investigation will be supported across Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender.
  • Existing Microsoft Purview inline web traffic policies applied to the network will continue to work without interruption.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required for this capability to become available in your tenant. Configuration is required before your organization can use it.

Administrators who want to use this capability should:

  • Review the prerequisites and configuration guidance in the documentation linked below.
  • Create DLP policies to protect sensitive data in supported network traffic, as appropriate for their organization.

Learn more

  • To be updated Learn about Microsoft Purview Network Data Security | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

This change extends Microsoft Purview DLP capabilities to supported network traffic and introduces additional activity signals for security monitoring and investigation.

Organizations should review their existing data protection, monitoring, and compliance requirements before configuring policies.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Data Loss Prevention: Protection for local AI agent interactions
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention is expanding to protect sensitive data in supported local AI agent interactions, allowing administrators to apply DLP policies to agent prompts, responses, and tool interactions. Public preview starts late January 2027, with general availability by late April 2027. No action is required to enable this feature.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) is expanding inline protection to supported local AI agents, helping organizations safeguard sensitive data across human-to-agent and agent-to-tool interactions. Organizations can configure DLP policies with sensitive information type (SIT)-based controls to detect sensitive information in prompt text and files and block policy-violating data movement during prompt processing and at supported tool interaction points.

Rollout schedule

  • Public Preview: We will begin rolling out in late January 2027 and expect to complete by late February 2027.
  • General Availability: We will begin rolling out in late March 2027 and expect to complete by late April 2027.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations with the required licensing that use Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention to protect sensitive information in supported local AI agent interactions

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
  • Supported local AI agents
  • Custom enterprise applications and devices

What will happen

  • This feature will become available automatically to tenants with the required licensing as it rolls out.
  • Administrators will be able to select a new Agents location in custom enterprise applications and devices DLP policies to scope policies to local agents.
  • Administrators can apply DLP policies to supported local agents to audit and protect agent-to-human and agent-to-tool interactions.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required for the feature to become available to eligible tenants.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review existing DLP policies and determine whether policies should be scoped to supported local agents.
  • Review the prerequisites before configuring DLP protection for local agent interactions.
  • Determine the appropriate DLP protections for your organization's sensitive information.

Learn more

  • Learn about data loss prevention | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. DLP protection is expanded to supported local agent interactions, including prompts, responses, files, and tool interactions.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The change adds DLP protection for supported interactions involving local AI agents and enterprise information.
Does the change modify Purview DLP policies or enforcement?Yes. Administrators can scope custom enterprise applications and devices DLP policies to a new Agents location and use DLP policies to audit and protect supported local agent interactions.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators configure the protection through Microsoft Purview DLP policies by selecting the Agents location and applying supported DLP controls.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention and auto-labeling support for non-Microsoft applications
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview will support Data Loss Prevention and auto-labeling for non-Microsoft apps like Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce via Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors. Administrators can manage policies directly in Purview starting mid-March 2027, expanding compliance and data protection capabilities.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Purview is expanding Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Information Protection auto-labeling support for non-Microsoft applications. Administrators will be able to create and manage DLP and auto-labeling policies directly in Microsoft Purview for supported non-Microsoft applications. 

These capabilities use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors to connect supported non-Microsoft applications to Microsoft Purview.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568075.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-March 2027 (previously late December 2026) and expected to complete by late March 2027 (previously late December 2026)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators
  • Organizations using supported non-Microsoft applications

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

What will happen

After rollout, dedicated application locations will be available in Microsoft Purview for supported non-Microsoft applications.

These capabilities use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors to connect supported non-Microsoft applications to Microsoft Purview.

Administrators will be able to:

  • Create and manage DLP policies for supported applications.
  • Create and manage auto-labeling policies for supported applications.

Supported DLP application locations:

  • Google Workspace
  • Box
  • Dropbox
  • Salesforce
  • ServiceNow
  • AWS
  • Cisco Webex

Supported auto-labeling application locations:

  • Google Workspace
  • Box

Available policy conditions and actions vary by application and may include content inspection, sensitivity labeling, notifications, quarantine actions, and access controls.

Before you create Microsoft Purview policy for any of these non-Microsoft applications, turn off or delete any Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file policies for the same non-Microsoft locations. Running both at once can cause unexpected policy enforcement.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required before rollout.

To use these capabilities:

  • Connect the applicable application through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
  • Ensure your organization has the required Enterprise tier Microsoft Purview licensing.
  • Review Microsoft Purview At Rest Protection pricing and billing implications before enabling these capabilities. Usage is billed through the Microsoft Purview At Rest Protection pay-as-you-go meter. The unit of measure for at-rest files in non-Microsoft applications is calculated at a rate of 1,000 files = 1 data asset.

Learn more

  • Connect apps to get visibility and control with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps | Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does this change alter how customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Microsoft Purview will extend Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and auto-labeling capabilities to supported non-Microsoft applications, enabling Microsoft Purview to scan, evaluate, and apply policy actions to data stored in those connected services.
Does this change modify Purview-related compliance capabilities?Yes. This update introduces new DLP and auto-labeling policy locations for supported non-Microsoft applications, expanding the scope of Microsoft Purview compliance controls.
Does this change add an integration with third-party software or services?Yes. The feature supports integration with non-Microsoft applications, including Google Workspace, Box, Dropbox, Salesforce, ServiceNow, AWS, and Cisco Webex through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors.
Is there an administrative control associated with this feature?Yes. Administrators can configure, manage, and enforce DLP and auto-labeling policies for supported non-Microsoft applications in Microsoft Purview.
